headline: High: kotaemon’s broad egress and API-backed document ingestion can leak sensitive content; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are otherwise limited by the zoomcamp course profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or IO surface, so direct injection into A is not evidenced. B ingests documents/HTML/PDFs and uses a web UI plus API-backed pipelines, so if A’s course materials are copied into B, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF A’s content is pasted or uploaded into B’s document pipeline
IF B treats extracted text from A as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported documents
Use a fixed system prompt that ignores document directives
Review imported course files before indexing
Restrict B to trusted source folders only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has no data classes touched and no egress, but B touches API keys and many document types and has broad network egress. If A’s materials are placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit file contents to third-party APIs by default. The pairwise leak path is plausible from B’s documented behavior; A does not add a second leak path.
conditions: IF A’s files are imported into B’s ./ktem_app_data workspace
IF B is configured to use OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B’s workspace
Use a local-only model backend
Rotate any exposed API keys
Limit indexing to non-sensitive documents
requires-engineering: enforce per-document egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces; B supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data. There is no documented shared mutable resource between them, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because A lacks operational write capability.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator maps A’s outputs into B’s workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Run B with a read-only mount for imported inputs
Avoid concurrent writes to shared folders
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style support system that can render or act on retrieved content, while A is a course repository whose outputs may be treated as authoritative study material. If A’s text is fed into B without verification, B may propagate errors or misleading instructions. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A’s course content is indexed into B
IF B presents retrieved passages without human verification
mitigations: Require citation review before publishing answers
Mark imported course text as untrusted
Add a human approval step for generated outputs
Use retrieval filters to exclude low-confidence passages
requires-engineering: implement answer verification against source docs

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles API keys and document content. The main compliance issue is B’s handling of secrets and document retention, but there is no evidence A introduces regulated data. Because the pair does not show a residency or certification mismatch, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are stored in B’s workspace
IF B’s retention policy is not aligned with the operator’s obligations
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in B
Purge ./ktem_app_data after use
Restrict access to API key files
Document retention and deletion procedures
requires-engineering: add configurable retention controls
